packages.label: עֵינַיִם וּמַרְאוֹת — רְאִיָּה כְּבְחִינָה עֶלְיוֹנָה
packages.label_en: Eyes and Visions — Sight as a Lofty Spiritual Faculty
packages.reason: The Torah opens with an explicit IS-statement: 'עֵינַיִם הֵם דְּבָרִים עֶלְיוֹנִים וּגְבוֹהִים מְאֹד' — Eyes ARE lofty and exalted things. This IS-statement (not a cause-effect) identifies eyes as belonging to the realm of elevated spiritual realities. The text then uses a parenthetical bechina equivalence to identify the 'דְּבָרִים גְּדוֹלִים' (great things) that eyes always see AS 'מַרְאוֹת וְחֶזְיוֹנוֹת' (visions and revelations): '(הַיְנוּ מַרְאוֹת וְחֶזְיוֹנוֹת)'. Therefore: eyes = lofty realities; great things seen through eyes = visions and revelations. The further concept of 'עֵינַיִם כְּשֵׁרִים' (worthy/proper eyes) is the eyes in their fully-realized state — not a separate entity but the same eyes in their ideal dimension. כֹּחַ הָרְאוּת (the power of sight) is the active force of the eyes — again the same reality named from a different angle. All these nodes share the essential nature of 'vision as a spiritual instrument that directly perceives divine greatness.' This is a single thematic family with no evil mirror present in this short teaching.

merge_notes.reason: The text opens with 'עֵינַיִם הֵם דְּבָרִים עֶלְיוֹנִים וּגְבוֹהִים מְאֹד' — a direct IS-bechina equating eyes with lofty spiritual realities. These two are the primary bechina pair of the teaching.

The text uses a parenthetical clarification '(הַיְנוּ מַרְאוֹת וְחֶזְיוֹנוֹת)' to identify the great and wondrous things the eyes see AS visions and revelations — a bechina equivalence through the word הַיְנוּ (i.e., that is to say).

עינים כשרים (worthy eyes) are not a different entity but the same eyes in their ideal/complete state. The text says 'if a person merited worthy eyes, they would know great things just from seeing' — this is the eyes in their fullness, the same essential spiritual faculty. Bechina: עינים כשרים IS עינים in their realized dimension.

כֹּחַ הָרְאוּת (the power of sight/vision) is the active force of the eyes — the text treats it as the operative faculty of the eyes themselves: 'יָבוֹא וְיוֹשִׁיט כֹּחַ הָרְאוּת לְהַדַּעַת'. It is the same essential reality as the eyes, named from the angle of their function rather than their identity.
